name: c
help: claudewheel - TUI launcher for Claude Code with profile, model, and directory selection

health.name: health
health.help: run diagnostic health checks on profiles, tokens, and hooks, then exit

config.name: config
config.help: open the ~/.claudewheel/ config directory in your $EDITOR

versions.name: versions
versions.help: list all installed Claude Code versions, marking the current symlink target

install.name: install
install.help: download and install a specific Claude Code version

args.name: version
args.help: semver version string to download and install (e.g. 2.1.119)

grants.name: download
grants.reason: installs an executable fetched from the Claude Code release bucket

uninstall.name: uninstall
uninstall.help: delete an installed Claude Code version binary from the versions directory

args.name: version
args.help: semver version string to remove (refuses if it is the current symlink target)

reset-options.name: reset-options
reset-options.help: delete options.json so it regenerates from defaults

show.name: show
show.help: print a summary of current segment selections, theme, and recent directories

migrate.name: migrate
migrate.help: move session data files from one profile to another, optionally filtered by UUID

args.name: src
args.help: source profile name whose sessions will be moved (e.g. work)

args.name: dst
args.help: destination profile name to receive the migrated sessions (e.g. personal)

args.name: uuid
args.help: UUID substring to migrate only matching sessions; when omitted, every session moves

stats.name: stats
stats.help: report shared-store stats and clean up legacy data

mv.name: mv
mv.help: rename a project directory and migrate session data

flags.name: post-hoc
flags.help: skip filesystem rename, migrate sessions only (directory already renamed); when omitted, the directory is renamed too

args.name: old
args.help: current path of the project directory to rename (absolute or relative)

args.name: new
args.help: target path for the renamed project directory (absolute or relative)

import.name: import
import.help: import session data from an external Claude Code directory

flags.name: reid
flags.help: assign new UUIDs to sessions that collide with existing local sessions; when omitted, a collision is reported instead

flags.name: from
flags.help: original project path as recorded in the source session data (repeatable)

flags.name: to
flags.help: local directory path that corresponds to the --from path on this machine (repeatable)

args.name: source
args.help: path to the source directory (e.g., /path/to/backup/.claude)

deploy-hooks.name: deploy-hooks
deploy-hooks.help: deploy built-in hook scripts to the ~/.claudewheel/scripts/ directory

flags.name: all
flags.help: deploy every known hook script from the built-in registry at once; when omitted, the positional name selects one script

flags.name: force-overwrite
flags.help: overwrite existing hook scripts on disk instead of skipping them; when omitted, an existing script is left alone

args.name: name
args.help: name of the specific hook script to deploy (omit to use --all)

patch-profiles.name: patch-profiles
patch-profiles.help: reconcile every managed profile and shared-settings.json to EXACTLY the canonical guardrail model (hooks, disallowedTools, permissions deny/ask); prunes drift and user-added extras -- the old additive, extras-preserving behavior is gone. Deploys any missing guardrail hook scripts. The 'default' profile (~/.claude) is never touched. Preview with --dry-run; writing needs a terminal or --approve-consequential.

reconcile-permissions.name: reconcile-permissions
reconcile-permissions.help: reconcile every managed profile and shared-settings.json to EXACTLY the canonical guardrail model (hooks, disallowedTools, permissions deny/ask made exact; allow keeps only its non-conflicting entries); prunes all drift and user-added extras. The 'default' profile (~/.claude) is never touched. Pass --dry-run to preview the per-target diff without writing; writing needs a terminal to confirm at, or --approve-consequential.

flags.name: profile
flags.help: reconcile only this single profile; when given, shared-settings.json is left untouched (omit to reconcile every profile AND shared-settings.json)

purge-plugins.name: purge-plugins
purge-plugins.help: remove the Claude Code plugin tree from the selected profiles: the official-marketplace clone and every plugin installed from it, six to ten megabytes per profile. Opt-in and separate from the canonical reconciliation, which is exact and would otherwise delete plugin state on every run. Names the marketplaces and plugins it finds before removing them; --dry-run reports the inventory without touching anything. New launches do not collect a new tree -- the launch environment suppresses the auto-install, one-way per profile. The 'default' profile (~/.claude) is never touched.

flags.name: target
flags.help: which profiles the operation applies to

choices.name: profile
choices.help: target one profile, by name

flags.name: value
flags.help: name of the profile to target (e.g. work, personal, research)

choices.name: all-profiles
choices.help: target every registered profile at once

launch.name: launch
launch.help: start the interactive TUI launcher to select a profile, model, and directory

flags.name: session
flags.help: which session this launch starts in

choices.name: cont
choices.help: continue the most recent conversation in the current directory

choices.name: resume
choices.help: resume one specific session

flags.name: value
flags.help: session to resume, by UUID or by title; an empty string opens Claude Code's own picker

choices.name: print-prompt
choices.help: run one prompt in non-interactive print mode and exit

flags.name: value
flags.help: the prompt to run non-interactively

choices.name: picker
choices.help: browse this profile's sessions and pick one to resume

choices.name: new-session
choices.help: start a new session (what a bare launch does)

flags.name: profile
flags.help: preset the Profile segment to this value, skipping TUI selection for it

flags.name: github
flags.help: preset the GitHub account segment to this value, skipping TUI selection for it

flags.name: model
flags.help: preset the Model segment to this value (e.g. opus, sonnet), skipping TUI selection

flags.name: directory
flags.help: preset the Directory segment to this path, skipping TUI selection for it

flags.name: mcp
flags.help: preset the MCP mode segment to this value, skipping TUI selection for it

flags.name: permissions
flags.help: preset the Permissions segment to this value, skipping TUI selection for it

flags.name: set
flags.help: set any segment value as KEY=VALUE (e.g. -s version=2.1.119); repeatable

flags.name: client
flags.help: launch target client (one of: claude, miniclaude). When omitted, the interactive launcher prompts with a Client step (cursor on config default_client, else claude) and non-interactive launches use default_client. Passing it explicitly skips that step. 'miniclaude' launches the miniclaude REPL instead; version and strict-MCP selections, config default_flags, and the disallowedTools list are claude-client-only

grants.name: exec-client
grants.reason: the launcher replaces this process with the selected client binary

profile.name: profile
profile.help: create, inspect, rename, delete, and manage Claude Code profiles and their stored tokens

create.name: create
create.help: run the create-profile wizard in one continuous alt-screen session: prompt for the profile name, config directory and launch options, write the profile directory together with its symlinks into the shared store, then drive an interactive Claude Code OAuth login so the profile is authenticated before you leave. Requires a real terminal, and prints the summary and auth outcome afterwards

grants.name: auth-login
grants.reason: the wizard drives an interactive Claude Code OAuth login for the new profile

delete.name: delete
delete.help: remove a registered profile: hand its directory to saferm, which archives it (the stored token among it) and then removes it, unlink its shared-store symlinks, drop its options.json registration, and clear any last_config reference in state.json. Prints the archive handle that restores it. Refuses a profile holding a live interactive Claude Code session unless --force-delete (background jobs and daemons do not block it), and takes conversation history only with --force-delete-data. saferm must be installed: without it the deletion would be irreversible, so it is refused rather than performed

flags.name: force-delete
flags.help: delete anyway when the profile holds a live interactive Claude Code session (background jobs and daemons never block deletion)

flags.name: force-delete-data
flags.help: delete even when shared-dir names hold REAL data instead of symlinks; this DESTROYS that data (e.g. conversation history)

args.name: name
args.help: name of the profile to delete (e.g. work, personal, research)

grants.name: archive-delegation
grants.reason: hands the whole profile directory, its stored OAuth token included, to saferm, which archives it and then removes it

show.name: show
show.help: print a detailed report for one profile: whether its directory exists on disk, whether it is registered or pinned in options.json, the state of its stored token, its resolved configuration and the session data it holds. Inspects default (~/.claude) like any other profile, and exits non-zero when the name matches no directory, registration or token

args.name: name
args.help: name of the profile to inspect (e.g. work, personal, default)

rename.name: rename
rename.help: move a profile to a new name, taking its directory (with the token stored inside it), its options.json registration and its session data with it. Validates that the old name exists, that the new one is free in both the directory tree and the options file, and that it fits the lowercase-letters-digits-hyphens charset. Refuses a profile holding a live interactive Claude Code session, and the reserved name default

args.name: old
args.help: current name of the profile to rename (must be an existing, non-running profile)

args.name: new
args.help: new name for the profile (lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens; must be unused)

fix-auth.name: fix-auth
fix-auth.help: repair one profile's authentication: strip the session credentials that shadow its stored long-lived token so the token is used again. Says so plainly when there is nothing to repair, and refuses a name with no profile directory behind it

args.name: name
args.help: name of the profile to repair: its shadowing session credentials are removed

set-plan.name: set-plan
set-plan.help: declare which plan a profile's Claude account is on, without a prompt. Claude Code resolves its subscription tier from the launch environment and only from there when auth is a stored setup token, so an undeclared profile launches with the tier null and tier-dependent features failing closed. Writes both plan fields into the profile's token entry, leaving the token itself alone; the interactive picker in the create flow and the pre-launch prompt write exactly the same thing

args.name: name
args.help: name of the profile to declare a plan for (e.g. work, personal)

args.name: plan
args.help: the plan this profile's Claude account is on; each one stores a subscription type and, where Claude Code has one, a rate-limit tier

choices.help: Max 20x (subscriptionType=max, rateLimitTier=default_claude_max_20x)
Max 5x (subscriptionType=max, rateLimitTier=default_claude_max_5x)
Pro (subscriptionType=pro, no rate-limit tier)
Team (subscriptionType=team, rateLimitTier=default_claude_max_5x)
Enterprise (subscriptionType=enterprise, no rate-limit tier)

check-tokens.name: check-tokens
check-tokens.help: read every discovered profile's own stored OAuth token and validate each one against the Anthropic API, then print a table of profile name, status and a truncated token preview. The status distinguishes a valid token from an invalid one, an unreachable API and an indeterminate answer, and profiles holding no token are listed too

permission.name: permission
permission.help: add, remove, and list permission rules across Claude profiles

add.name: add
add.help: Add a permission rule to a profile's settings.json. Takes a category (allow, deny, or ask) and a rule string such as Bash or Read(//home/**). Writes the rule into the specified category array. Use --profile to target a single profile or --all-profiles to apply the rule across every registered profile. Skips duplicates if the rule already exists in the category.

flags.name: target
flags.help: which profiles the operation applies to

choices.name: profile
choices.help: target one profile, by name

flags.name: value
flags.help: name of the profile to target (e.g. work, personal, research)

choices.name: all-profiles
choices.help: target every registered profile at once

args.name: category
args.help: permission category to add the rule to: allow, deny, or ask

args.name: rule
args.help: permission rule string to add (e.g. Bash, Read(//home/**), Edit)

remove.name: remove
remove.help: Remove a permission rule from a profile's settings.json. Takes a category (allow, deny, or ask) and the exact rule string to delete. The rule is removed from the specified category array and the file is saved. Use --profile to target a single profile or --all-profiles to remove the rule from every registered profile. Reports whether the rule was found.

flags.name: target
flags.help: which profiles the operation applies to

choices.name: profile
choices.help: target one profile, by name

flags.name: value
flags.help: name of the profile to target (e.g. work, personal, research)

choices.name: all-profiles
choices.help: target every registered profile at once

args.name: category
args.help: permission category to remove the rule from: allow, deny, or ask

args.name: rule
args.help: exact permission rule string to remove (must match an existing entry)

list.name: list
list.help: List permission rules from a profile's settings.json. Displays rules in grouped or flat format controlled by --format. Use --category to filter output to a single category (allow, deny, or ask). Use --profile to inspect a single profile or --all-profiles to show rules from every registered profile, with each profile's rules displayed under a header. The framework-owned --json answers a machine instead: one envelope carrying every listed profile, whatever --format the human form would have used.

flags.name: format
flags.help: output format: grouped (indented tree) or flat (tsv)

choices.help: one indented block per category, one rule per line
one tab-separated category-and-rule pair per line

flags.name: category
flags.help: restrict output to a single permission category (allow, deny, or ask)

flags.name: target
flags.help: which profiles the operation applies to

choices.name: profile
choices.help: target one profile, by name

flags.name: value
flags.help: name of the profile to target (e.g. work, personal, research)

choices.name: all-profiles
choices.help: target every registered profile at once
